description: (0.5.0, Draft) A capabilities document whose `limits` sub-object carries an unknown field. From 0.5.0 `limits` is OPEN (additionalProperties: true; acdp-capabilities.schema.json and the openness map in RFC-ACDP-0007 §3.3.1), like the document top level (caps-006 / schema-004). A consumer implementing 0.5.0 MUST tolerate the unknown field: it MUST NOT reject the document and MAY ignore the field. Through 0.4.0 `limits` was CLOSED and this same document was a schema_violation; a consumer implementing only 0.4.0 or earlier is held to that earlier expectation (expected.pre_0_5_0).

expected.consumer_action: Pass the schema check, ignore (or retain in an extension map) the unknown `limits` key, and continue with the operation that required fetching capabilities. Known limits fields are still validated: a known field with an invalid value remains a schema_violation (caps-005, caps-007, caps-008, schema-014).

pre_0_5_0.note: Through 0.4.0 `limits` was closed (additionalProperties: false), and this fixture pinned rejection.

expected.rationale: Limits are advisory pacing hints a consumer can safely ignore. While `limits` was closed, every new limit was a hard break for every deployed consumer and forced a coordinated rollout per field. Opening it relaxes a constraint: no previously valid document becomes invalid, and limits fields added after 0.5.0 never need staging for 0.5.0+ consumers. Companion to caps-006 / schema-004, which pin the open top level.
